title: ailang fmt Adoption — Discoverability + Opt-in Harness Hooks

premise_flags.note: Phase-2 execution gate is now SATISFIED. M-AILANG-FMT-PHASE2 landed iter-63 (PR #414, squash 3815ba617). The doc's '⛔ Execution Gate', '⛔ Quorum Block', and Rev-3 hard-gate sections are now HISTORICAL. Doc is cleared to plan. M1's gate-check task is retained as a live sanity tripwire, not a blocker.

CRITICAL check requested in the planning directive. The shipped binary's exit-code contract MATCHES the doc's hook-contract assumption EXACTLY. Verified live in cmd/ailang/fmt.go header (lines 24-37) and by execution: 0=success/canonical, 1=--check drift, 2=operational error (usage/read/print/round-trip/envelope/write; comment-refusal for inline-interior lands here too), 3=input parse error. Live test: non-parsing file `let x = = =` -> exit 3; canonical --check on examples/ai_modes.ail -> exit 1 (drift). The hook's silent-vs-surface distinction (exit 3 silent, all else surface) is therefore sound as written. NO premise conflict. See also phase-2 impl doc lines 168-169.

Mark approved the SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILL escalation (doc lines 54-56). Quorum is CLOSED by Mark decision. The doc's shipped hook script (lines 282-291) currently sends only `kill` then unbounded `wait` — this is the exact defect that must be fixed. Sprint MUST land the escalation `kill "$PID"; sleep 1; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$PID"`. Precedent verified live: .claude/skills/mission-control/SKILL.md:254 uses `kill; sleep 2; kill -9`.

acceptance_criteria: Makefile gains a standalone `fmt-check` target running `ailang fmt --check` over examples/**/*.ail + stdlib/**/*.ail; exits 1 and lists drifted paths on drift, 0 when canonical. `make ci` is byte-identical before/after (target NOT wired into ci).
`make fmt-check` run once and the drift count recorded as an informational baseline in the implementation report (mass reformat is explicitly out of scope).

scripts/hooks/format_ail.sh created following format_go.sh's matcher + always-exit-0 + additionalContext-surfacing mechanism, but NEVER discarding fmt stderr (no `2>/dev/null` on the `ailang fmt` invocation — only `2>&1` into the capture file).

APPROVED FIX LANDED: the bounded-timeout guard escalates SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILL before wait — `kill "$PID"; sleep 1; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$PID"` (per Mark decision, quorum closed). The doc's shipped script snippet (kill-then-unbounded-wait) is the pre-fix version and MUST NOT be copied verbatim.

Silence audit: the shipped hook's `ailang fmt` invocation has NO `2>/dev/null`; jq presence is probed up front (`command -v jq`) and the first jq call carries no stderr suppression; the silent branch is pinned to exactly exit 3.
.claude/settings.json registers the hook under hooks.PostToolUse with matcher Edit|Write, alongside the existing Go entry; the Go hook still fires unchanged.

Manual tests pass: (a) edit a valid .ail file -> formatted, turn not blocked; (b) non-parsing .ail -> exit 3 silent defer, file untouched, turn not blocked; (c) unreadable/chmod file -> exit 2 advisory context surfaced, turn not blocked; (d) stub `ailang` that sleeps past the 10s deadline -> fmt SIGKILLed after grace, file byte-identical, timeout advisory surfaced, turn not blocked (proves the escalation reaps a SIGTERM-ignoring process).
Idempotence spot-check: running the hook twice on the same file — second run is a no-op.
`make test` green (regression tripwire — nothing in internal/ changed).
